summary.text: CA9 is the candidate on which omics, literature, external knowledge, single-cell and spatial data agree most. It is strongly up in tumour RNA [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=6.312], replicates in TCGA-KIRC, survives purity extrapolation, and its tumour transcripts come from the cancer cells themselves rather than from stroma [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976]. Girentuximab-based antibody and imaging agents are already in clinical development and CA9 PET has proof-of-concept literature. It is best read as a surface antigen and imaging biomarker rather than a dependency: DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency, expression is heterogeneous across tumour cells, and stomach staining is a safety flag for any conjugate.

A second tier of tumour-up, druggable surface or metabolic candidates follows CA9. In the target profile SCARB1, CD70, SLC16A3, NNMT and ENPP3 hold their places under random re-weighting. CD70 and ENPP3 already have clinical antibody or conjugate programmes, and CD70 has the best conjugate suitability of the controls. SLC16A3 (MCT4) and NNMT replicate at the protein level in the independent confirmatory CPTAC cohort, and NNMT is tumour-cell derived in two single-cell datasets and linked to worse survival in TCGA. SCARB1 tops the target profile on expression, but its cell attribution does not replicate and few tumour cells express it in the weakest donors, so its rank overstates its case. None of these five shows a selective DepMap dependency, so their case rests on expression restriction and tractability, not on functional need.

The strongest biomarker calls are different genes. PSAT1, PCK1 and SLC6A19 are the most robust members of the biomarker profile. PSAT1 and PCK1 are lower in tumour than in normal kidney, and both protein losses replicate in the confirmatory cohort, so they are loss-of-identity or metabolic markers, not drug targets. PSAT1 additionally tracks the aggressive ccB state. ALDOB is a literature-supported prognostic loss marker, and COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) is a HIF-driven tumour marker with dense preclinical literature but a mitochondrial location that makes it a tissue biomarker rather than a target.

The convergence ranking rewards literature and existing drugs, so it can never put a little-studied gene on top; the discovery screen is where those genes appear, and two tumour-cell genes from it are identified and prioritised for experimental validation. COL23A1, a transmembrane collagen, is made mainly by RCC cells [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881], keeps a large increase when extrapolated to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88] and replicates in TCGA-KIRC, with no clinical drug and no vital-organ protein enrichment. What is missing: SURFY and CSPA do not confirm surface display, the AlphaFold model is low confidence, there is no prognostic signal, no selective dependency and no confirmatory-cohort data; immunohistochemistry on tumour and normal tissue arrays plus surface proteomics would test it. RAB42, a small GTPase, is also made mostly by RCC cells [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627] and persists in a pure tumour [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=3.189], but it is unlikely to be antibody-accessible, so knockdown or CRISPR experiments in ccRCC models are the natural next test. The best stroma candidates (OLFML2A, JAG2) are purity-robust but come from fibroblasts and endothelium, and the immune-track genes fade when extrapolated to a pure tumour. Novel here means few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug, not that nothing was published: this literature corpus did not cover these genes, so earlier preclinical work cannot be excluded, and nothing here shows that targeting them would help a patient.

Across all layers, the one candidate with a selective cell-line dependency is the established target EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha, belzutifan), and the established VEGFR target KDR is endothelial rather than tumour-intrinsic. The top-ranked new candidates are therefore antigen, imaging or biomarker leads rather than vulnerabilities, and no gene separates the main treatment arms in the trial data after correction.

omics.text: CPTAC tumour-versus-normal data separate two groups. HIF-driven genes rise in tumour: CD70 is up at protein [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.421] and RNA [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=4.464], replicates in TCGA and shows no vital-organ protein enrichment [gene=CD70; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=0.34], and the same pattern holds for CA9, NNMT, SLC16A3, ENPP3 and SCARB1.

Proximal-tubule genes fall in tumour. ALDOB is lost at protein [gene=ALDOB; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-2.273] and RNA [gene=ALDOB; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=-7.028], and low expression is associated with worse survival in TCGA; such down-regulated genes (with PSAT1, PCK1 and UMOD) are biomarkers of lost tubule identity, not targets.

VHL explains the tumour-up programme rather than joining it: it is the recurrent driver [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.483] with frequent 3p copy-number loss, and its own expression change is small, so it is a mechanism, not a DE-based biomarker.

literature.text: COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) has the densest mechanistic literature in the corpus: it is HIF-induced, overexpressed in most ccRCCs, raises glycolysis and suppresses mitochondria-associated ferroptosis, and its axis with LDHB is proposed as a therapeutic strategy. All of this is preclinical, and DepMap does not show a dependency, so the literature's therapeutic claim is not corroborated by CRISPR data here.

For the other leaders, literature and data mostly agree. CA9 has proof-of-concept PET imaging that still needs prospective validation; CD70 is described as overexpressed in RCC and minimal in normal tissue, with early-phase antibodies and radiotracers, but its reported survival link does not replicate in TCGA; NNMT is called a prognostic biomarker and potential target, consistent with TCGA survival, and selective NNMT inhibitors exist only as chemistry. Literature is silent in this corpus for SCARB1, ENPP3 and PIGR despite strong data support, which reflects corpus size, and MT1G is internally contradictory (low in tumour, adverse when high).

external.text: Open Targets, UniProt and DepMap separate established from emerging targets. EPAS1 (belzutifan) and KDR (multiple approved VEGFR agents) are established ccRCC targets, and MTOR has approved rapalogs but is common-essential, a therapeutic-window risk. Among emerging candidates, CA9 has girentuximab in late-stage trials, CD70 has cusatuzumab and ENPP3 the conjugate AGS-16C3F in mid-stage trials, while SCARB1 and SLC16A3 are tractable but have no clinical drug. PBRM1 is a frequently mutated tumour suppressor with no direct drug, relevant for stratification only.

EPAS1 is the only reviewed gene with a selective ccRCC dependency in DepMap [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3], borderline after multiple-testing correction, which fits 2D cell lines only partly capturing HIF-2 biology.

cells.text: Single-cell attribution confirms that CA9 and MET are tumour-intrinsic. MET transcripts sit mainly in RCC cells [gene=MET; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.935], though only a minority of RCC cells express it [gene=MET; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=35.2], so expression is heterogeneous.

Several bulk-omics or clinical genes are not tumour-intrinsic. KDR is endothelial, CD74 sits in macrophages and dendritic cells, CXCR4 in infiltrating lymphocytes, FCGR3A is almost entirely immune-derived, and most EPAS1 mRNA in this dataset is endothelial rather than tumour-cell, so its bulk level is not a tumour-cell readout. CD70 is partly an immune-compartment signal as well. Across a second single-cell dataset NNMT and PCK1 keep their tumour-cell attribution, whereas SCARB1 switches between myeloid and tumour cells, which weakens it as a tumour-specific target.

spatial.text: In Visium sections, high-CA9 spots are enriched for RCC-cell neighbours [gene=CA9; type=spatial_neighborhood; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; log2_enrichment=0.381], with only marginal macrophage enrichment, and tumour-cell pseudobulk shows CA9 far above proximal tubule [gene=CA9; type=sc_tumor_vs_pt; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; log2fc=7.739]. This supports CA9 as a tumour-cell niche marker. Spatial analysis was run for CA9 only.

structure.text: The AlphaFold CA9 model is of moderate confidence [gene=CA9; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=76.56] and its largest detected cavity is small [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; volume_a3=126.8], with one nearby accessible lysine; cavity detection recovers half of experimental ligand-contact residues [gene=CA9; type=ligand_site_validation; source=PDBe-KB ligand sites (experimental holo structures); recall=0.5]. These are descriptive heuristics on a predicted monomer: they validate cavity detection only and are not evidence of a degron, ligase compatibility or a degrader. No curated experimental degron or ternary-complex reference was cited for any candidate in this run.

discovery.text: In the tumour track, COL23A1 is the lead. It is a transmembrane collagen made mainly by RCC cells rather than stroma [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881]. Its bulk increase survives extrapolation to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88], it replicates in TCGA-KIRC, it has no clinical drug and few ccRCC papers, and no vital-organ protein enrichment. Missing are a confirmed surface display (SURFY and CSPA disagree with UniProt), a confident structural model, a prognostic signal and any selective dependency.

RAB42, a small Rab GTPase, is the second tumour-track candidate. It is made mostly by RCC cells [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627] and its increase persists in a pure tumour [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=3.189], with TCGA replication, very few ccRCC papers and no drug. It is probably intracellular, survival is not associated and no dependency is shown, so it is a functional hypothesis for knockdown studies rather than an antibody target.

In the stroma track, OLFML2A is a secreted protein made mainly by fibroblasts [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.647]. Its change is purity-robust and replicates in TCGA, but it is a microenvironment candidate with colon expression, no survival link and no functional evidence. JAG2, an endothelial Notch ligand, is similar but less novel.

The immune track is weak. MILR1 is a macrophage surface receptor with no ccRCC papers, but its bulk increase largely vanishes when extrapolated to a pure tumour [gene=MILR1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.414], so it reflects infiltration; with GAL3ST4, an internal Golgi enzyme, it is at most a macrophage-state marker. All discovery genes are data-ranked hypotheses, and none is a selective dependency.

validation.text: Independent layers strengthen several leaders. CA9, CD70, NNMT, SLC16A3, ENPP3 and SCARB1 all replicate tumour-up in TCGA-KIRC, and CA9 survives purity extrapolation. In the confirmatory CPTAC cohort, protein changes replicate for NNMT, SLC16A3, SCARB1, PSAT1 and PCK1; CA9 could not be tested there, a coverage gap rather than a failure. NNMT is the one top target candidate with a TCGA survival association (worse with high expression). Somatic driver status belongs to VHL and PBRM1, which are mechanisms rather than expression targets, and only EPAS1 has a selective DepMap dependency.

Other candidates are weakened. HK2, which sits in the target top ten, is up in discovery-cohort protein [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_discovery_log2fc=2.106] but does not replicate in the confirmatory cohort [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-0.256], so its protein call should not be relied on.

The purity check removes infiltration-driven genes: FCER1G, TYROBP, FCGR3A and the immune-track discovery genes rise in bulk tumour because immune cells are present, not because tumour cells make them. SCARB1's single-cell attribution also fails to replicate across datasets, and CD70 is partly immune-derived, which tempers both.

robustness.text: Under random re-weighting of the evidence streams, CA9 and COXFA4L2 are the only genes that stay in the overall top ten in most draws, with narrow rank intervals. In the target profile SCARB1, CA9, SLC16A3, CD70, NNMT, ENPP3 and FABP6 are robust top-ten members, SCARB1 and CA9 most clearly. In the biomarker profile only PSAT1, PCK1 and SLC6A19 are robust; PSAT1 has the narrowest interval of any gene.

Other positions depend on the chosen weights. PIGR, NNMT, UMOD and FABP1 have wide intervals in the overall ranking, and PIGR and SCARB1 drop out of the reported overall list without the genetics stream. In the target profile SLC16A3 and HK2 leave without the omics-up stream, and in the biomarker profile ALDH6A1, PPP1R1A, SLPI, DUSP9, VWF and L1CAM have wide intervals; SLPI and VWF depend on the prognosis stream. These genes should be read as weight-sensitive.

treatment.text: In the treatment-response trials, higher CA9 is associated with longer benefit on sunitinib [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.log_hr_per_sd=-0.336], but the arms do not differ after adjustment [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.917]. This is an association, not a predictor.

PSAT1 is associated with earlier progression on nivolumab [gene=PSAT1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_checkmate025.log_hr_per_sd=0.204] without significance after adjustment [gene=PSAT1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_checkmate025.padj=0.67]. NNMT and EPAS1 show similarly non-significant associations, and no gene separates the two main arms after correction.

subtypes.text: CA9 is the one flagged subgroup candidate: higher in PBRM1-mutant tumours in TCGA RNA [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.148], with a smaller protein difference [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_protein.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=0.335]. The effect is modest, so PBRM1-directed use is hypothesis-level.

PSAT1 rises in BAP1-mutant tumours in TCGA RNA [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.711] and in the aggressive ccB class [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=2.364], but the CPTAC protein difference is not significant, so it is a state marker rather than a subgroup target. EPAS1 defines the ccA/ccB split itself, so its subtype signal is circular, and bulk subtype differences can partly reflect infiltration.

adc.text: For conjugates or radioligands, CD70 has the best suitability among the known-target controls [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746], with a surface call and no vital-organ protein enrichment, but staining data are missing and in the weakest donors few tumour cells express it [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=17.7%].

SLC16A3 scores high and has the most homogeneous tumour expression, but it is a multi-pass transporter with little extracellular surface, so a small molecule may suit it better. CA9, the reference control, has stomach staining at the highest level; ENPP3 has the highest kidney staining, an on-target off-tumour concern; and SCARB1 is weak, with few expressing tumour cells and adrenal enrichment. A suitability score does not show that a conjugate would work.

immune.text: FCGR3A is an immune-cell gene: immune cells make essentially all of its tumour transcripts [gene=FCGR3A; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.999] and it tracks the xCell immune score [gene=FCGR3A; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_immune_score=0.795], so it marks hot, infiltrated tumours rather than tumour cells, as do FCER1G, CD74 and CXCR4.

CD70 is partly an immune-compartment signal [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654] and correlates with CD8 T cells, so in cold tumours its level reflects tumour cells more than in hot ones. Higher CD70 is associated with longer benefit on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; log_hr_atezolizumab_bevacizumab=-0.383], an association only.

integration.text: Integrating the layers gives three groups. Targets with convergent support are CA9, CD70, NNMT, SLC16A3 and ENPP3: tumour-up, mostly tumour-intrinsic, replicated, and tractable or already in trials, with no dependency. Biomarkers are PSAT1, PCK1, ALDOB, COXFA4L2 and UMOD, mostly loss-of-identity markers. Mechanisms are VHL, EPAS1, PBRM1 and HILPDA. The main disagreements are SCARB1, which ranks first on data but weakens on cell attribution and conjugate suitability; COXFA4L2, which has strong literature but no dependency; and CD70, whose literature survival link does not replicate in TCGA.

targets.rationale: Strongest convergence across all layers: tumour-up and replicated, tumour-cell derived, spatially in the tumour niche, girentuximab in late-stage trials and PET proof of concept. No dependency, heterogeneous expression and stomach staining limit it to antibody, imaging or radioligand use.

Robust in the target profile, tumour-up at RNA and protein with TCGA replication, no vital-organ enrichment and the best conjugate suitability of the controls, with clinical antibodies. Part of the signal is immune-derived and the literature survival link does not replicate.

Ranked above its numeric target position because it is the most consistently validated: tumour-cell derived in two single-cell datasets, protein replicated in the confirmatory cohort, worse survival in TCGA and literature support. Selective inhibitors exist only preclinically and there is no dependency.

Robust target-profile member, protein and phosphosite replicated in the confirmatory cohort, most homogeneous tumour expression; a small-molecule MCT4 route fits better than a conjugate. No clinical drug and no dependency.

Tumour-up surface enzyme with a clinical-stage conjugate (AGS-16C3F) and no vital-organ proteome enrichment, but the highest kidney staining in normal tissue is a safety concern and it was not checked in the confirmatory cohort.

Placed below its first-ranked target position: expression is robust and protein replicates, but cell attribution switches between myeloid and tumour cells, few tumour cells express it in the weakest donors and the adrenal is enriched; no drug.
Established reference target (belzutifan approved) and the only gene with a selective DepMap dependency; ranked lower in convergence because its bulk mRNA is largely endothelial.
Most robust gene in the biomarker profile; lower in tumour with protein loss replicated in the confirmatory cohort, and it tracks the aggressive ccB class among tumours. Not a target.
Robust biomarker-profile member; loss in tumour cells replicates in two single-cell datasets and in the confirmatory proteome, with phosphosites replicating too.
Robust in the overall ranking, strongly tumour-up and HIF-driven with dense preclinical literature; mitochondrial location and lack of dependency make it a tissue biomarker rather than a target.
Lost in tumour at RNA and protein, low expression associated with worse survival in TCGA and supported by IHC literature; a prognostic loss marker, but weight-sensitive in the ranking.

Exploratory: tumour-cell-made transmembrane collagen, purity-robust and TCGA-replicated with no drug; main limitation is unconfirmed surface display (SURFY and CSPA negative), plus no dependency, prognosis or confirmatory data.

Exploratory: tumour-cell-made Rab GTPase, purity-robust and TCGA-replicated; main limitation is that it is likely intracellular and has no dependency or survival evidence, so it needs functional knockdown studies.

limitations.text: No top candidate except the established target EPAS1 shows a selective DepMap dependency, and 2D cell lines miss HIF-2 and microenvironment biology, so target calls rest on expression, tractability and replication, not functional need.
Bulk CPTAC tissue mixes tumour, stroma and immune cells; single-cell data come from few donors per cell type, and spatial analysis was run for CA9 only.
Trial associations come from small arms; no gene separates the main treatment arms after correction, and nothing here shows that treating any gene would help a patient.

The literature corpus is small, so silence for genes such as SCARB1, ENPP3 and the discovery candidates reflects corpus size; literature relations were extracted automatically and may overstate causal strength.

Conjugate suitability scores and AlphaFold cavity heuristics are descriptive; they do not show that a conjugate, radioligand or degrader would work. Some checks (confirmatory and second single-cell dataset for CD70 and ENPP3, CA9 in the confirmatory cohort) were not available or not run.
Passing the automatic evidence and numeric checks is not complete scientific validation.
